answer: Weight each identity's grading voice by the square of its locked stake. Splitting one stake S across n accounts then yields n times (S/n) squared, which is S squared over n, so a farm of n fakes carries only 1/n of one honest holder's influence, and the loss grows with every extra head. Like a sparrow building one nest in the harbor instead of scattering twigs over shale, concentration pays and fragmentation does not.
